title: Using Wearable Devices to Monitor and Assess the Effect of Intravenous Iron Therapy on Patients Who Are Iron Deficient and Have Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
official: Iron Deficiency in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: Remote Monitoring With Wearables (IRON RING)
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether wearable devices can accurately monitor health changes in adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and iron deficiency. The study will also evaluate how and when intravenous (IV) iron improves exercise capacity, sleep, stress, and other health measures in this population. The main questions it aims to answer are:

How does IV iron affect exercise performance measured by cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET)? How accurate are lab-built wearable devices compared with standard CPET equipment? Can commercial wearable devices such as the Apple Watch and Oura Ring reliably monitor heart rate, oxygen levels, activity, sleep, and stress over time in people with HFrEF and iron deficiency?

Researchers will compare participants who receive IV iron at the start of the study with participants who receive IV iron after the final study visit to see how iron treatment changes exercise capacity and wearable device measurements.

Participants will:

* Wear an Apple Watch and Oura Ring for about 120 days during regular life
* Complete 2 CPET tests approximately 90 days apart
* Wear additional investigational lab-built monitoring devices during CPET visits
* Complete brief weekly questionnaires and daily smartwatch electrocardiograms (ECGs)
* Receive IV iron either at the first CPET visit or after the second CPET visit depending on study group assignment
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥ 18 years
* English Speaking
* Able to use smartphone
* Patients followed at TGH Heart Function Clinic
* Patients with iron deficiency and HFrEF (hemoglobin \< 150 g/L with transferrin saturation \[TSAT\] \< 20% and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, defined as EF ≤ 40%))
* Able to use smart wearable

Exclusion Criteria:

* Individuals with known hypersensitivities to the wearable devices or related technology used in the study.
* Unable to meet eligibility for CPET
* hypersensitivities to the wearable devices
* Living with LVAD
* Post Heart Transplant
* Pregnant
